messages:
maria: FYI — customer reported they didn't see the 'act_as' field on RBAC grant events, and we had an ingest spike during the canary that caused ~30s ack delays. Need a quick plan for schema validation + how we handle high-volume audit traffic.

sam: A couple quick asks: 1) Add a JSON Schema for audit events (required fields + enums). 2) Prod-side validator that can reject or coerce before we index. 3) Customer-facing validation endpoint so they can pre-check event shape.

anita: Also flag: KMS per-event envelope vs field-level encryption. Field-level calls KMS per event and adds CPU. Envelope + per-batch CEK reduces KMS calls massively. Bench: our PoC went from ~6ms KMS latency/event -> ~0.15ms amortized when batching 500.

leo: Indexing strategy question: per-tenant indices or unified index with tenant as field? Per-tenant isolates costs but explodes index count for 1000s of tenants. Unified index requires careful shard sizing and more complex retention. I lean time-windowed indices (daily/week) + tenant shard routing for hot tenants.

ingest-bot: alert: ingest_queue_depth=12000, bulk_fail_rate=0.6%, avg_bulk_latency=1.2s as of 1781234700 :rotating_light:

jen: For backpressure we should: token-bucket at front proxy (fast reject), dynamic batching (grow batch up to 1k on backpressure), and fallbacks: drop non-critical audit subtypes (metrics/debug) to cold store. Pseudocode for batching config:

```
# ingest collector config
max_batch_size: 1000
max_batch_time_ms: 150
kafka_produce_timeout_ms: 500
kms_batch_mode: true  # envelope keys per batch
priority_event_types: ["rbac_grant", "token_issue", "auth_failure"]
```

sam: +1 on envelope KMS. Also we need customer-facing validation to be strict for prioritized events (RBAC, token ops) and lossy/defaulted for low-value telemetry.

dave: Cost back-of-envelope: assume 2k events/s avg, 172.8M events/day ~5.2B/month. If avg raw event = 1KB and ES storage after compression ~0.55x, that's ~2.7 TB/month. ES storage @ $0.12/GB/mo -> ~$324/mo just for raw storage. Add indexing IO and replica overhead ~x2 -> ~$650/mo. For 1000 tenants the ops cost climbs fast. We need retention policies and tiering.

maria: Action items: 1) sam -> draft JSON Schema + validator by EOD. 2) anita -> KMS envelope implementation plan + perf numbers. 3) leo -> index sharding proposal + cost model. 4) jen -> backpressure config + proxy token-bucket PR. 5) dave -> storage/cost spreadsheet with 3 scenarios (best/expected/worst).

sam: I'll post a minimal JSON Schema snippet here in a sec.

sam: ```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["ts","event_type","actor","resource","severity"],
  "properties": {
    "ts": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
    "event_type": {"type":"string"},
    "actor": {"type":"object"},
    "resource": {"type":"object"},
    "act_as": {"type":"string"}
  }
}
```

leo: small note: add schema version field so we can roll forward without breaking older records. e.g., schema_v: "2026-03-01".

anita: For KMS PR we should support two modes: kms_mode: ["envelope","per_field"] and default to envelope. Provide opt-in per-customer for per_field if they require FIPS/HSM validations.

jen: Regarding runtime backpressure signals: expose metrics: ingest_queue_depth, avg_bulk_latency, producer_retries. Hook these to a simple state machine: NORMAL -> SLOWDOWN -> REDUCE_TO_CRITICAL -> DROP.

maria: Great. If anyone needs a quick pairing sesh for tests (esp. KMS perf or bulk bench), ping me. Also we should draft a short customer note about validation expectations and that heavy telemetry may be sampled.

dave: I'll start the cost spreadsheet and share a link. If we plan to tier cold storage (S3) for older audit events, add retrieval cost estimates.

sam: One more: add an ingest schema conformance metric (pct_valid_events) and alert if < 97% for priority events.

maria: Thanks all. Will update roadmap ticket with owners. :white_check_mark:
